title: MOT Retest NI: Rules, Costs and the Free Retest Window
excerpt: If your vehicle fails its MOT in Northern Ireland, here's how the DVA retest works - when it's free, when a fee applies, and how to prepare for a first-time pass.
contentHtml:
If your vehicle fails its MOT in Northern Ireland, you can get a free partial retest if you take it back to the same DVA test centre by the end of the next working day. Return it later than that and a full retest fee applies. MOTs in NI are run by the DVA (Driver & Vehicle Agency), not the DVSA that covers England, Scotland and Wales - the rules are similar but not identical.

When an MOT retest is free in NI

After a failure, the DVA offers a partial retest that only rechecks the items that failed, rather than the whole vehicle. It's free when:

  • you return the vehicle to the same test centre, and
  • you bring it back by the end of the next working day.

Miss that window and you'll pay for a full retest at the standard MOT fee. So if a repair is quick, getting the car back promptly can save you the second fee.

How the NI retest process works

When your vehicle fails, the DVA gives you a failure notice (a VT30) listing every reason for failure. Get those specific items repaired, then rebook the retest at the same centre. Because NI test-centre appointments can be booked up well in advance, it's worth reserving a retest slot as early as you can rather than waiting until the repair is done.

How to book an MOT retest in NI

You book or rebook an MOT retest in Northern Ireland through the nidirect MOT booking service online, or by phone. After a failure, rebook at the same test centre so you can still use the free partial retest if you make the next-working-day window. NI test slots often fill up well ahead, so reserve the retest as early as you can - ideally as soon as you know what needs fixing - rather than waiting until the repair is finished.

How much does an MOT retest cost in NI?

A partial retest is free inside the next-working-day window at the same centre. Outside that, you pay for a full retest at the standard DVA MOT fee. The DVA sets and periodically reviews these fees, so check the current price on nidirect before you book - but the key saving is simple: get the car back promptly and the retest can cost you nothing.

Common reasons vehicles fail an MOT

Most failures come from a small set of areas - and many are cheap to fix before the test:

  • Lighting and signalling (blown bulbs are one of the most common fails)
  • Tyres below the 1.6mm legal tread, or with damage
  • Brakes - worn pads, imbalance, or a handbrake that won't hold
  • Suspension and steering wear
  • Windscreen, wipers and washers
  • Exhaust and emissions

Check the MOT history before you rebook

Before a retest, it's worth looking at the vehicle's full MOT history. RegScan shows every past test, the mileage recorded, and the advisories noted each year - free, no sign-up, using official data. If the same advisory keeps appearing, that's often the very thing that has now tipped into a failure. Check your vehicle to see its history and recurring advisories.

How to pass first time

A quick pre-test check of lights, tyres, wipers, washer fluid, number plates and warning lights clears the most common failures before you ever reach the centre. Fixing an advisory early - rather than letting it become a failure - is almost always cheaper than a fail plus a retest.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is an MOT retest free in Northern Ireland?

A partial retest is free if you return the vehicle to the same DVA test centre by the end of the next working day. After that, a full retest fee applies.

Who runs MOT tests in Northern Ireland?

The DVA (Driver & Vehicle Agency) runs MOT testing in Northern Ireland, unlike Great Britain where it's the DVSA and approved garages.

How long do I have to get an MOT retest in NI?

To keep the retest free, bring the vehicle back to the same centre by the end of the next working day. There's no free retest after that window - you'd pay the full fee.

How do I book an MOT retest in Northern Ireland?

Book or rebook through the nidirect MOT booking service online or by phone, and choose the same test centre you originally failed at so you can qualify for the free partial retest.

How much is an MOT retest in NI?

Free as a partial retest if you return to the same centre by the end of the next working day; otherwise you pay the standard DVA MOT fee for a full retest. Check the current fee on nidirect.

Can I drive my car if it failed its MOT in NI?

Only in limited cases. If your previous MOT is still valid and the failure had no dangerous defect, you may drive it; otherwise you can generally only drive to a booked repair or retest. Never drive a vehicle with a dangerous defect.

How do I check my car's MOT history?

Enter your registration on RegScan to see the full MOT history, mileage and advisories free, using official data.
